verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
MinIO is gone from the code, from the applications state and from Nomad.
The backup job runs as `backup-s3` from `default/backup-s3/*`, ov-dash is back, and the gates are green on a stamp I ran myself.
The plan and eval amendments are sound: `mc` is an S3 client pointed at SeaweedFS, and each name the r1 allowlist keeps has a stated reason that does not depend on MinIO running.
Nothing blocks.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree passed `pre_commit`, `cli_tests` and eval row r1 (stamp 64c1255701e334a4582c54eb2b4fb9d13b3c1b50264c8d1b76affd2617499c71).
The pinned `kmctl check` (v0.10.0) reports all checks passed.
Diff: I read the staged change against HEAD 9fe1ebe.
`git diff --cached main` also shows main's later harness commits (justfile, apm, .opencode), which do not belong to this ticket.

I read every code, test and Terraform hunk in full, and the docs that carry claims: the three new how-tos, the workload-identity explanation, gcs-backups, monitoring, edge-routes, run-a-backup-job-on-demand, ADR 0018, `components/minio.md`, the manifesto and the summary.
r1 (command): `cli/tests/test_no_minio.py` walks `deployments/`, `bootstrap/`, `cli/src` and the Dockerfile.
It fails on any line that names MinIO (case-insensitive) once a per-file allowlist pattern is removed.
The allowlist is narrow: `minio/` only in backup-s3.hcl and restore-s3.hcl, `minio_data` only in services.tf, `minio-go` only in tempo.hcl, and the mc URL plus its comment only in the Dockerfile.
A second test proves the scan reads backup-s3.hcl, so an empty walk cannot pass.
It checks the row's fails_when.
My own grep finds only the allowed names, and the gitignored applications lock file no longer names minio.
r2 (judgment): I checked it live myself rather than trusting the report.
`terraform state list` in applications has 0 `minio`/`module.buckets` addresses.
`terraform plan -lock=false` reports "No changes" in applications.
In infrastructure it lists only the 15 `null_resource.firewall` replacements that the `always_run` trigger forces on every plan.
The removed blocks used `destroy = false`, so no bucket or object was deleted, and spike 4 records the evidence.
r3 (judgment): `nomad job status minio` and `backup-minio` return 404.
`backup-s3` is a registered periodic job with its next launch at 03:00, and spike 4 records the forced run's exit 0.
In Vault, `default/backup-s3/gcs` and `default/backup-s3/seaweedfs` are live.
`default/minio/localstack` and all of `default/backup-minio/*` have no metadata left, so they were purged.
r4 (judgment): the three MinIO how-tos are replaced by SeaweedFS ones.
They match the code (`local.seaweedfs_keyless_jobs`, tempo's three env vars, the `#keyless-seaweedfs-access` anchor) and keep the how-to skeleton.
`workload-identity.md` describes SeaweedFS, and MinIO appears only in a "Before SeaweedFS" paragraph.
`components/minio.md` is `status: deprecated` with a "Superseded by SeaweedFS" lead, because the bundle has no superseded status.
ADR 0018 records the removal and the rejected volume-destroy.
No docs page tells a reader to use MinIO, and no link points at a deleted page.
Correctness spots: `seaweedfs_buckets = local.buckets` matches the old drop-filter result, since memex and mlflow-artifacts left the catalog.
`backup_s3` reads the renamed paths.
The comment edit inside `rules_hcl` in `machine_roles.tf` rewrites the deploy policy, but that apply already ran and the plan is clean.
The memex staging note points at a real SeaweedFS port and Consul lookup.
None.
The plan says `cli/tests/test_health_rules.py` should follow the rename, but it still parametrizes `backup-minio`.
That job name comes from a captured `/v1/jobs/statuses` fixture, which also still lists `promtail`.
Renaming the job inside a recorded capture would falsify it, so leaving it is right.
The plan line was too broad.
The plan's Outcome bullet still lists only the backup prefix and mc as the names left.
The amended r1 row also allows restore-s3, `minio_data` and `minio-go`.
The row is the contract and it is right, so the plan text is just behind.
Soft-deleted versions remain in Vault at `default/<job>/minio` (for example `default/loki/minio`), and the MinIO users still exist inside `minio_data`.
Nothing serves them while MinIO is stopped.
`minio-volume-destroy` is the natural place to purge both.
